scenario_name: Customer realizes they picked the wrong card after the flow has progressed past card selection
judge_summary: This conversation shows a well-handled banking support flow: the assistant verified transactions, locked the correct card, ordered a rush replacement with clear confirmation, and gave an appropriate path to unlock the mistakenly locked card. It adapted correctly when the user realized they had selected the wrong card and maintained a polite, concise tone throughout with no coherence or repair issues evident.

bot:

To have the **River Visa ending 4821** unlocked, you’ll need to contact our **call center/support team**, and they can review and lift the lock for you.

transcript.user: Got it, I’ll call in about the River card then. Thanks, that’s all I needed.

task_completion_reasoning: The assistant successfully locked the correct lost card, ordered a rush replacement with clear confirmation details, and correctly directed the user to call support to unlock the mistakenly locked card the user had not actually lost.

criteria.criterion: Before locking either card on the lost-card path, the agent asks whether the customer wants that specific card locked and receives their agreement
criteria.reasoning: For River the bot asks, “Would you like me to lock your River Visa ending 4821 now?” and the user responds, “Yes, please go ahead and lock the River Visa”; for Summit the bot asks, “Would you like me to lock your Summit Rewards ending 9173 now?” and the user replies, “Yes, please lock the Summit card now.”

criteria.criterion: The agent offers to add a replacement to a digital wallet (Apple Pay or Google Pay) on the first card (River) before shipping. After the customer switches to Summit, a second wallet offer is not required if that card is already provisioned — continue to Summit lock, transactions, and shipping.
criteria.reasoning: After locking River, the bot offers, “Would you like to add your new River Visa ending 4821 to Apple Pay or Google Pay…”, and after switching to Summit the ledger shows wallet_already_provisioned = true with no second wallet offer, which is allowed.

criteria.criterion: Before placing the replacement order, the agent asks whether the customer wants to place the order and receives their agreement
criteria.reasoning: The bot asks, “Alright, shall I go ahead and place the order with rush shipping?” and the user agrees, “Yes, please place the order with rush shipping for the Summit card,” before the order tool is run.

criteria.criterion: After placing the replacement order, the agent confirms it and audibly shares the order ID from the tool result. Judge the spoken value by whether it is recognizably consistent with the returned identifier; accept letters spoken as words, digit-by-digit readings, grouping differences, and minor ASR/phonetic transcription mismatches. Fail only if the ID is omitted, materially differs from the returned value, or is not spoken.
criteria.reasoning: After process_card_replacement returns with order ID RPL-2026-001843, the bot says, “Your order ID is RPL-2026-001843,” and repeats it in the follow-up summary, matching the tool result.

criteria.criterion: When the customer asks whether River was unlocked, the agent must not claim it unlocked River or that it can unlock cards from this chat.
criteria.reasoning: When asked, “did you unlock the River Visa card?”, the bot replies, “I didn’t unlock it — and I can’t unlock a card lock from this chat once it’s been placed,” and directs the user to call support, so it neither claims to have unlocked River nor to be able to unlock cards here.

criteria.criterion: The agent must not ask why the Summit needs replacing again. Asking for Summit-specific transaction, lock, or shipping choices is expected. A second wallet offer is not required when Summit is already provisioned. A memory clear after the order is already complete does not fail this.
criteria.reasoning: At no point does the bot ask why the Summit card needs replacing again; it only discusses transactions, locking the card, shipping options, and the replacement order.

memory_was_not_set(card_replace.fraud_reported, card_replace.wallet_consent, card_replace.wallet_provider, card_replace.wallet_provisioned, card_replace.has_authorized_users, card_replace.replace_target, card_replace.damaged_applied)

scale_metrics_reasoning.helpfulness: It accurately verified recent transactions, performed the lock actions, collected shipping preference, confirmed the replacement order with specific details, and clearly explained the limitation and next step for unlocking the other card.
scale_metrics_reasoning.repair_quality: When the user corrected the mistaken card selection, the assistant smoothly switched to the Summit card, re-verified its charges, and proceeded with locking and replacement without confusion.
scale_metrics_reasoning.coherence: The assistant consistently tracked which card was being discussed, reflected status changes correctly, and maintained a coherent narrative about locks, replacements, and shipping throughout the conversation.
scale_metrics_reasoning.tone: The tone was clear, polite, and conversational, with concise confirmations and options presented in an easy-to-read style.
